title: Build a Preparation Plan from Interview Feedback
summary: Turn an interview or mock session into a focused cycle of practice and reassessment.
prerequisites: One interview, mock session or self-check result to review.
learningObjectives: Choose a small number of relevant priorities.

sections.heading: Capture evidence while it is fresh
body: After an interview, write down the questions you remember, the answers you gave and the moments where you were unsure. Do not claim to reconstruct every word. Label approximate notes as approximate and avoid copying confidential tasks or materials you are not authorised to retain. Your aim is to identify learning needs, not to build a leaked question bank.

Separate four kinds of issue: missing knowledge, weak application, unclear explanation and unfamiliar interview format. If you can define Queueable Apex but cannot explain retry behaviour, that is an application gap. If your answer is technically sound but takes five minutes to reach the point, the main improvement may be communication. Different gaps need different practice.

callouts.text: “I did badly” is not an actionable finding. Name the specific behaviour you want to improve.

sections.heading: Prioritise by relevance and evidence
body: Create a table with topic, observed difficulty, target-role relevance, practice task and verification. Choose two priorities for the next cycle. A repeated gap in the core responsibilities of your target role usually deserves attention before a niche topic that appeared once. Do not assume that a rejection was caused by the one answer you disliked; hiring decisions may include information you do not have.

For example, write: “Bulk Apex: I placed a query inside a loop during the exercise. Practice: aggregate input records and query related data once. Verification: run a test with 200 input records and explain the query count.” This is much clearer than “Review Apex.” It defines a behaviour, an action and evidence that the action helped.

sections.heading: Plan a small cycle with different activities
body: Use a short cycle that fits your schedule. One session can rebuild the concept from a primary source, another can implement a small example, and a third can explain a variation aloud. Leave time to review the result. Reading, coding and explaining expose different weaknesses; doing only one of them can create a misleading sense of progress.

A sample week might contain two forty-minute technical sessions and one twenty-minute mock discussion. Adjust the duration to your availability. The important part is completing a small loop: identify a gap, practise it, verify the result and reassess. Keep job applications moving at a realistic pace if you are actively searching; endless preparation can become a way to avoid testing your fit in the market.

callouts.text: Put one verification task on the calendar before adding more learning resources.

sections.heading: Reassess with a changed scenario
body: At the end of the cycle, solve a related problem with a different condition. If you practised a successful callout, try a timeout and duplicate response. If you studied sharing, explain what happens when a separate permission set grants a permission that is muted in a group. A changed scenario tests the mechanism rather than memorisation of a single answer.

Record the outcome as demonstrated, partly demonstrated or still unclear, with a short reason. Keep the original note so you can see what changed. If the topic remains unclear, reduce the scope and identify the missing prerequisite. If you can explain and demonstrate it, move to the next priority while scheduling occasional retrieval practice. The plan should evolve from evidence, not from a growing pile of bookmarks.

callouts.text: A completed preparation task includes an observed result and a decision about what to do next.

exercise.title: Apply this to your own search
exercise.brief: Turn one interview or mock session into a one-week preparation plan.
steps: Record the questions and uncertainties you remember.
Classify each gap as knowledge, application, explanation or format.
Choose two priorities related to your target role.
Schedule learning, implementation and explanation tasks.
Test a changed scenario and record the result.
acceptance: Each priority has a concrete practice task and a verification method.
The plan fits the time you actually have.
Reassessment uses a variation, not only the original question.

knowledgeCheck.question: Can you know why an employer rejected you without feedback?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Usually not. Record what you observed and avoid turning a guess into a confirmed cause.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why classify the type of gap?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Because reading documentation will not by itself fix every application or communication problem.

knowledgeCheck.question: When is a preparation task complete?
knowledgeCheck.answer: When you have performed the planned verification and recorded what it demonstrates and what remains unclear.

recap: Choose a small number of relevant priorities.
